0.title: How a menopause protein score was built
0.caption: Three-stage design linking blood proteins at menopause to later cognitive ageing and dementia risk. Numbers from Wood et al., Nature Medicine, 2026. Press a number to step through it.
steps: Discovery: serum from 80 women aged 43–58, staged with STRAW+10, showed menopause shifting inflammatory, synaptic, metabolic and Alzheimer's-linked proteins, tracking hormones more than age.
Replication: plasma from 2,814 age-matched women showed the same shifts, plus more inflammation and catabolism and signs of faster ageing across organs, including the brain.
A menopause proteomic score applied to four cohorts of 11,925 older women (mean ages about 61–72) went with greater cognitive ageing and higher dementia risk. Association, not proof of cause.

1.title: What else is in the human proteome
1.caption: Where single amino-acid variants come from and how many a proteogenomic survey found. Numbers from Tretyachenko et al., Nature, 2026. Press a number to step through it.
steps: A protein's sequence can change on the way from gene to protein: inherited or somatic DNA changes are genetic; mistranslation of the message is non-genetic.
Mining proteogenomic data from 29 healthy tissues found 13,910 variant peptides, 7,215 distinct single amino-acid swaps, sitting alongside the reference forms.
Variant abundances mirrored population frequencies, and hundreds of non-genetic variants recurred across people or fell at functional sites. Their function is mostly unproven.

2.title: How the TRI-611 molecular glue works
2.caption: TRI-611 glues ALK fusion proteins to a cellular disposal ligase; results so far are preclinical. From Conery et al., Nature, 2026. Press a number to step through it.
steps: TRI-611 glues the ALK fusion's kinase domain to CRBN, the substrate adaptor of the CRL4 ubiquitin ligase, at a degron interface away from the kinase's active site.
The ligase tags the fusion protein with ubiquitin for destruction. Every ALK fusion form tested was degraded, including inhibitor-resistant ones.
In preclinical models it shrank tumours under the skin and inside the skull, spared other kinases and CRBN neosubstrates, and with ALK inhibitors gave lasting regressions.

3.title: How TM184C was found and what it does
3.caption: Structure-first discovery of GPCR-like proteins and the roles of TM184C, shown in cells and yeast. From Lee et al., Nature, 2026. Press a number to step through it.
steps: Searching millions of AlphaFold2 models by shape found two 'superdark' seven-transmembrane families, TM184 and PRRT, that look like GPCRs though their sequences give little away.
Like receptors, they recruit beta-arrestin and are phosphorylated by GPCR kinases.
TM184C rides mobile vesicles along microtubules and promotes nanotube-like bridges through which cells share organelles, using its C-terminal tail and an arrestin-binding motif.
TM184C limits autophagic flux by curbing LC3B lipidation, and the human protein rescues autophagy defects in yeast lacking its counterpart, Hfl1.
